title: Freeze recovery inventory class contract and quarantine record
description: Objective: resolve the current contradictory inventory cardinality and define the durable fail-closed reconciliation/quarantine record the coordinator can persist. Deliverable: one canonical daemon recovery-inventory contract that maps every detailed external population to exactly one configured proof class, defines ABSENT/ADOPTED/QUARANTINED/UNKNOWN dispositions and upstream-code retention, and provides a frozen digest-verified persisted record bound to project, backup cursor/generation, selected incarnation/key epoch and quarantine refs. MEASURED GAP at HEAD c0c5929: design line 978 names seven populations, CORE-S14 names six grouped categories, @moe/runner exposes four combined node classes, adding scheduler resource yields five proof classes, the coordinator description lists six groups, and DoD demands seven generated classes; the runner collector rejects unknown/extra classes. No production quarantine/reconciliation record or sink exists. Consumer: task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa and downstream task-6f786c58cabf4f85be8ed4135e68a752. NOT in scope: enumerating providers, invoking adapters, allocating authority, or approving recovery.complete. Owned paths: focused daemon recovery contract/codec/persistence modules and tests, plus minimal store schema only if required. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: A frozen hand-written class/population mapping resolves the 4-runner/5-proof/6-scenario/7-population ambiguity: every design population is covered exactly once, no proof is duplicated to inflate cardinality, and unknown/duplicate/omitted/extra classes refuse with stable code/layer.

The contract defines canonical ABSENT, ADOPTED, QUARANTINED and UNKNOWN dispositions; ADOPTED requires exact restored intent plus current incarnation/key epoch, unmatched items can only quarantine/UNKNOWN, and no disposition invents history or retry authority.

A durable frozen reconciliation record binds project, backup cursor and generation, selected incarnation and key epoch, configured class mapping, source proof digests, every item disposition, retained upstream code/layer and quarantine refs; any byte change changes or invalidates its digest.

Missing inventory, incomplete coverage, non-fenceable state, artifact/key proof failure and unresolved items persist truth UNKNOWN with coordinator code UNKNOWN_TRUTH at RECOVERY_INVENTORY while retaining the precise upstream code/layer separately.
Persistence/reopen and hostile-byte tests drive the real store/codec surface, assert exact cardinalities and stable code/layer, and generated cases assert a non-zero exact population count.

Mutation drills alter canonical digest input and one adoption/incarnation comparison and turn named tests red; fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not satisfy the seven-population requirement by duplicating a combined runner proof; the mapping must be explicit and one-to-one at the semantic population level.
Do not narrow the design or accept caller-selected current binding; use exact selected store/anchor authority in consumers.
Retain upstream code and layer separately from the coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH/RECOVERY_INVENTORY answer; never restamp away provenance.
Shared schema changes require full regression and crash/reopen evidence.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the focused contract and exact LF NodeNext bridge. Freeze ordered proof classes as `PROVIDER_PROCESS_LAUNCH_LOCK`, `RESOURCE`, `WORKSPACE`, `INTEGRATION_TARGET`, `GIT_INTEGRATION_ON_DISK`, `ARTIFACT_OBJECT_STAGING`; freeze the seven design populations and the explicit class-to-population rows, with only the provider class containing two populations. Define closed proof/truth/disposition/result vocabularies, precise mapping error codes (`RECOVERY_INVENTORY_CLASS_EXTRA|UNKNOWN|DUPLICATE|OMITTED`), coordinator `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`, layer `RECOVERY_INVENTORY`, ledger upstream codes/layer, bounds, and immutable record/input/result types. Model terminal cancellation explicitly without granting retry/history authority; do not let Git/submodule evidence certify durable integration attempts or artifact-object evidence certify scheduler resources.
implementationPlan.note: Contract extended and the shared invariant surface landed. Contract gains exactly two closed-vocabulary codes: RECOVERY_INVENTORY_PROOF_TRUTH_CONTRADICTS (builder refuses a configured proof asserting COMPLETE while carrying an upstream refusal) and RECOVERY_INVENTORY_RECORD_INCOHERENT (decoder refuses self-consistent bytes whose SEMANTICS the builder could never have emitted). INCOHERENT is deliberately distinct from RECORD_NONCANONICAL (shape/keys/vocabulary/byte-spelling) and RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH (binding), so a green test proves WHICH of the three guards answered — the exact defect class that let these forgeries ship twice. New apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-inventory-invariants.ts (186 lines, LF bridge .js one-liner) is the ONE production home for: compareRecoveryReconciliationItems (class rank, then DECLARED population rank inside the class, then identity — population outranks identity so the mapping row order is the canonical order), orderRecoveryReconciliationItems, isCanonicalRecoveryItemSequence (strictly increasing AND class-scoped unique), isCanonicalRecoveryItemShape (the exact adjudicator-emitted required/forbidden field combinations per disposition), isCanonicalRecoveryProofSlot (the reserved sentinel may only ever be UNKNOWN + PROOF_MISSING/RECOVERY_INVENTORY), deriveRecoveryReconciliationTruth and sameRecoveryUpstream. The builder will EMIT with these and the decoder will RE-DERIVE against them, so the property is pinned on the production surface rather than on a test reimplementation. GOTCHA hit and worked around: the write path silently converts an intended `�` source escape into a real 0x00 byte (the same trap that produced the QA-flagged record.ts:164 blob) — the separator is therefore spelled String.fromCharCode(0), which is plain ASCII source with the identical runtime value. Verified 0 NUL bytes in the new file.

implementationPlan.description: Implement total record normalization/adjudication and its exact LF bridge. Validate hostile inputs with own enumerable data descriptors before property access; require the exact configured six-class set and normalize a missing/incomplete configured proof into its canonical UNKNOWN proof slot rather than shrinking the mapping. Bind each subject to its one mapped proof, project/project-tag, verified backup cursor+generation, selected anchor binding digest/incarnation/key epoch, source proof digest, restored-intent reference/digest, terminal proof or quarantine reference, disposition, and separate coordinator/upstream refusal tuples. Enforce: ABSENT only from complete negative proof; CANCELLED only from terminal cancellation proof; ADOPTED only when external/restored identity and both selected recovery refs match exactly; unmatched items only QUARANTINED or UNKNOWN; any incomplete/non-fenceable/artifact-or-key/unresolved fact makes the persisted truth `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`/`RECOVERY_INVENTORY`. Deep-freeze copied data and expose no secret/message bytes.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the strict canonical codec and exact LF bridge. Encode a versioned, fixed-key-order, bounded UTF-8 JSON body with deterministic class/population/item ordering; compute SHA-256 over every body field except `recordDigest`, then append that digest. Decode with fatal UTF-8, exact keys/vocabularies/bounds/cardinalities, re-derived six-to-seven mapping and disposition invariants, digest recomputation, and byte-for-byte canonical re-encoding so whitespace, key order, duplicate keys, extensions, truncation, or any semantic byte mutation cannot become an alternate authoritative record. Return the stable unreadable upstream code/layer under coordinator UNKNOWN rather than throwing or defaulting.
implementationPlan.note: Decoder now re-derives every builder invariant BEFORE the digest, and all 14 forgeries refuse. Guards added: (a) record truth and retained upstream are RECOMPUTED from the children via the shared deriveRecoveryReconciliationTruth and compared, so COMPLETE cannot survive an UNKNOWN proof or an unresolved item and the retained code cannot name the wrong cause; (b) the reserved sentinel slot must itself be UNKNOWN with PROOF_MISSING/RECOVERY_INVENTORY; (c) every item must carry the exact adjudicator-emitted required/forbidden field combination for its disposition; (d) the item sequence must be the single canonical order AND class-scoped-identity unique. Ordering of guards matters and is pinned: structure/semantics settle first, so DIGEST_MISMATCH can never shadow a semantic guard. Introduced RECOVERY_INVENTORY_RECORD_INCOHERENT as a code distinct from RECORD_NONCANONICAL; the two pre-existing hardening cases (item-vs-proof provenance, terminal disposition under an unknown slot) are semantic and now correctly answer INCOHERENT, and I added a NONCANONICAL positive control (duplicate JSON key) so a test can still prove the shape reader answered rather than the semantic one. SPLIT FOR THE PER-FILE CAP: codec.ts had reached 391 lines, so the strict readers moved to new recovery-inventory-reader.ts (266) with an LF bridge; codec.ts is now 158 and owns only the byte boundary (canonical field order, digest, encode, decode entry). Focused run: 4 files / 80 tests passed. FOREIGN CONDITION, disclosed and re-attributed: a peer landed RecoveryIncarnationBinding as a GENESIS|RESTORE discriminated union in the already-committed recovery-incarnation-contract.ts and is mid-flight on its consumers. That broke my owned recovery-inventory-ledger.ts:165, which read anchored.backupGenerationDigest. I fixed only my own file, with an `in`-narrowed read that treats the absent field as a refusal (BINDING_MISMATCH) — chosen over narrowing on `origin` because the peer's readAnchoredIncarnation does not yet emit the discriminant, so an origin-based guard typechecked but refused every real anchored binding and reddened 9 of my own ledger tests. The `in` form is correct under both the old and new runtime shapes and keeps the comparison fail-closed. Daemon typecheck is still red on EIGHT foreign paths I must not touch: index-surface.test.ts, recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts, recovery-incarnation.test.ts, recovery-incarnation.ts, recovery-key-provider.ts, recovery-succession.ts, restore-controller-commands.ts, restore-controller.ts. No owned path is on that list.

implementationPlan.description: Implement content-addressed durable persistence/readback and its exact LF bridge using only the existing public `SqliteEventStore` transaction surface—no schema change or raw SQLite. The write service must read the fixed ACTIVE recovery binding from the project store and the exact anchored incarnation, cross-check key epoch/project/backup generation, and only then build the record; it must accept no request-selected current refs. Commit canonical bytes once under a domain-separated record-digest aggregate with command kind `recovery.reconcile_external`, expectedVersion 0, exact domain schema/event IDs, and identical request/result/event bytes; exact retries replay one event. The reader addresses an explicit record digest (never an invented 'latest'), verifies the sole sequence-1 event plus decision trace/decision bytes and codec/digest/aggregate identity, and maps absent, conflicting, malformed, or unverifiable evidence to `UNKNOWN_TRUTH`/`RECOVERY_INVENTORY` while retaining `RECORD_NOT_FOUND|UNREADABLE|CONFLICT` at `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER`. R3 may later bind this immutable digest; this task grants no recovery.complete authority.
implementationPlan.note: Durable path re-verified against the repaired decoder and extended. The ledger already satisfied this step (content-addressed write under a domain-separated record-digest aggregate at expectedVersion 0, exact-retry replay onto one event, digest-addressed readback with no invented 'latest', close/reopen and second-handle visibility, RECORD_NOT_FOUND|UNREADABLE|CONFLICT retained at RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER under coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH/RECOVERY_INVENTORY, and no recovery.complete authority) and its 15 tests drive a real temporary-file SqliteEventStore. Added the case that was missing for DoD 5: a SELF-CONSISTENT semantic forgery driven through the real durable path. A legitimately committed record is mutated to claim truth COMPLETE over an UNKNOWN proof carrying an INVENTORY_ADAPTER refusal, re-digested with production recoveryReconciliationDigest, encoded with the production encoder, and committed under the aggregate for the digest it NOW hashes to — so the attacker controls the bytes and the address, the stored evidence is internally consistent, and neither the digest guard nor the aggregate-identity guard can answer. readRecoveryReconciliation refuses with RECORD_UNREADABLE at RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER under coordinator UNKNOWN_TRUTH/RECOVERY_INVENTORY, which proves the new decode-layer re-derivation is reachable through persistence rather than only in unit tests. Paired with a positive control in the same test: the untouched record at its own digest still reads back ok, so the refusal is the forgery and not a broken durable path. Also folded in the ledger's binding-union adaptation from step-5 (the `in`-narrowed anchored generation read). Focused run: 4 files / 81 tests passed.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review done and ELEVEN byte-restored mutation drills all turned their named production-surface test red. Each drill asserted three things, because two of the three failure modes are invisible otherwise: the mutation actually changed the file (sha256 before != after, so a missed anchor cannot read as green), the named test went red, and the file restored to the exact original sha256. Drills: D1 derived truth, D2 derived upstream code, D3 sentinel slot, D4 disposition field shape, D5 item order, D6 class-scoped identity uniqueness, D7 builder COMPLETE+upstream refusal, D8 delete the PROVIDER_RUN population edge, D9 omit keyEpochRef from the digest body, D10 bypass incarnation equality, D11 bypass key-epoch equality. Suite exit 0; all six touched sources verified byte-identical afterwards. D1 CAUGHT A REAL TEST DEFECT and is the reason the drill was worth running: deleting the truth comparison left "refuses a child proof UNKNOWN under record truth COMPLETE" GREEN, because the neighbouring derived-upstream guard answered for it — the exact "refusal answered by another guard" failure this epic's rail 6 warns about. I added an isolating case, "refuses truth COMPLETE while the retained code already admits an incomplete proof", which keeps the upstream code the derivation would produce so the upstream guard agrees and stays silent and only recomputing truth can refuse; D1 then went red. Review checks: zero NUL bytes across all 16 owned files (record.ts:164 repaired); zero CR bytes in every source and all eight .js bridges, each an exact one-line LF re-export, verified with a positive control that the CR probe does fire; production line counts contract 287, record 188, subject 300, proofs 166, codec 146, reader 266, ledger 289, invariants 186 — all below the 400 cap, and codec came DOWN from 391 via the reader split; no secret, key, nonce or adapter message is serialized (the only `payload` references are the record's own canonical bytes and the result/event byte equality check); ledger tests track every SqliteEventStore handle and close both before reopen/delete for Windows; the combined provider proof is still stored once over two populations. Scratch drill script removed — no evidence file remains. reopenReason: The prior unknown/duplicate proof-row, item/proof digest, and Proxy defects are repaired, and daemon/store tests are green, but fresh production-surface probes found the persisted contract still fails open on semantic contradictions. The builder accepts COMPLETE proof evidence that simultaneously carries an upstream refusal and silently drops that provenance. More critically, after mutating a legitimate production record, recomputing its digest with recoveryReconciliationDigest, and encoding it through the production encoder, the production decoder accepted: child proof UNKNOWN under record truth COMPLETE; a reserved no-proof sentinel slot claiming COMPLETE; ABSENT without a terminal proof; ADOPTED without an intent digest; reversed item ordering; and a duplicated class-scoped identity. These are self-consistent hostile bytes, so digest verification cannot excuse the absent semantic guards. Re-derive the builder invariants on decode and add exact RECOVERY_INVENTORY code/layer regressions that recompute the digest so DIGEST_MISMATCH cannot shadow them. Also replace the literal NUL source byte at record.ts:164 with a textual escape. Verification disclosure: the exact requested chain stopped at daemon typecheck on foreign uncommitted packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launcher.ts:151 TS2339 errors; independently-run daemon tests passed 68/1230 and store tests passed 40/453. The foreign typecheck red is disclosed but is not one of the owned defects.

planningNotes.risks: The runner registration factories preserve only aggregate inventory code/layer, not the deeper Git/artifact observer refusal; retain exactly what production exposes and never invent deeper provenance. `readCurrentRecoveryAuthenticationBinding` collapses missing/unreadable to null, so the ledger must fail closed with a local upstream code rather than claim a selected binding. Production probe supplied RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN/INVENTORY_ADAPTER and buildRecoveryReconciliationRecord returned ok:true, record.truth:'COMPLETE'. Refuse the contradictory tuple or normalize it to UNKNOWN without losing the original code/layer; pin the exact builder refusal/answer.

readRecord checks only top-level truth/coordinator/upstream co-presence; it does not derive truth from child proofs/items or require RECOVERY_UNKNOWN_PROOF_DIGEST slots themselves to be UNKNOWN. With a freshly recomputed valid digest, both (a) one UNKNOWN proof under record COMPLETE and (b) a sentinel COMPLETE proof with itemCount 0 decoded ok:true COMPLETE. Re-derive these invariants before digest acceptance and assert exact RECORD_NONCANONICAL/RECOVERY_INVENTORY (or another frozen code/layer).

readItems does not enforce exact disposition field combinations. Recomputed-digest bytes with ABSENT and terminalProofDigest:null, and ADOPTED with restoredIntentDigest:null, both decoded ok:true COMPLETE. Require all builder-emitted required/forbidden fields for ABSENT, CANCELLED, ADOPTED, QUARANTINED, and UNKNOWN, with exact production-decoder reason/layer tests.

The decoder preserves arbitrary item order and never rejects a duplicate class-scoped identity. Reversing all items or inserting a duplicate and adjusting itemCount, then recomputing the digest, decoded ok:true COMPLETE. Enforce the builder's canonical class/population/identity order and uniqueness on decode; tests must recompute the digest and assert the semantic guard rather than DIGEST_MISMATCH.

The identity-key template contains a literal 0x00 byte. Git classifies the production TypeScript blob as binary (byte scan NUL=1; git diff reports Bin), eliminating normal line diff/blame/merge. Preserve the separator semantics but spell it as a textual source escape such as \\u0000, then prove the committed blob contains zero NUL bytes.

rejectionHistory.reason: The prior unknown/duplicate proof-row, item/proof digest, and Proxy defects are repaired, and daemon/store tests are green, but fresh production-surface probes found the persisted contract still fails open on semantic contradictions. The builder accepts COMPLETE proof evidence that simultaneously carries an upstream refusal and silently drops that provenance. More critically, after mutating a legitimate production record, recomputing its digest with recoveryReconciliationDigest, and encoding it through the production encoder, the production decoder accepted: child proof UNKNOWN under record truth COMPLETE; a reserved no-proof sentinel slot claiming COMPLETE; ABSENT without a terminal proof; ADOPTED without an intent digest; reversed item ordering; and a duplicated class-scoped identity. These are self-consistent hostile bytes, so digest verification cannot excuse the absent semantic guards. Re-derive the builder invariants on decode and add exact RECOVERY_INVENTORY code/layer regressions that recompute the digest so DIGEST_MISMATCH cannot shadow them. Also replace the literal NUL source byte at record.ts:164 with a textual escape. Verification disclosure: the exact requested chain stopped at daemon typecheck on foreign uncommitted packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-launcher.ts:151 TS2339 errors; independently-run daemon tests passed 68/1230 and store tests passed 40/453. The foreign typecheck red is disclosed but is not one of the owned defects.

rejectionHistory.reason: Fresh foreground verification is green, but adversarial production-surface probes reproduced three fail-closed gaps. The builder silently accepts unknown and duplicate supplied proof-class rows, accepts a subject whose sourceProofDigest contradicts its mapped COMPLETE proof and still returns truth COMPLETE, and lets a throwing Proxy trap escape instead of returning the stable typed refusal. These gaps violate the closed-class contract and allow unverifiable provenance to gain COMPLETE truth. Validate supplied proof rows as a closed unique set, cross-link each subject digest to its mapped proof, contain/reject proxies before reflective access, and add exact code/layer regressions against the production builder.
failedDodItems: DoD 1: unknown/duplicate/extra proof classes must refuse with a stable code/layer.
DoD 3: item dispositions and source-proof digests must form a verifiable durable record.
DoD 4: unverifiable evidence must remain UNKNOWN with retained provenance.

issues.description: normaliseProofs uses supplied.find and silently discards all unmatched rows. Production probes with a seventh proof {class:'ALIEN', ...} and with a duplicate of proofs[0] both returned ok:true, truth:'COMPLETE', proofCount:6. Validate the supplied proof array itself; refuse unknown, duplicate, and extra class rows with distinct stable RECOVERY_INVENTORY code/layer, and add production-surface tests that pin which guard answered.

A subject is adjudicated without verifying subject.sourceProofDigest equals the sourceProofDigest of its mapped configured proof. Mutating only the first subject digest to deadbeef... while its class proof remained c0... returned ok:true and truth:'COMPLETE', persisting contradictory provenance. Fail closed (typed refusal or UNKNOWN as specified) with an exact reason/layer and test a positive nonzero sweep across mapped classes.

exactDataRecord invokes Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors on unknown input without Proxy containment. A Proxy whose ownKeys throws caused buildRecoveryReconciliationRecord to throw 'trap-executed', contradicting the claimed hostile-input refusal and the stable-result rail. Reject transparent proxies and contain throwing/revoked proxies before reflective traps; assert immutable UNKNOWN_TRUTH/RECOVERY_INVENTORY with upstream RECOVERY_INVENTORY_INPUT_INVALID/RECOVERY_INVENTORY.
